# ↪️ Pull Request

Adds support for Manifest V3 to `@parcel/transformer-webextension`.
Closes #6079
Fixes #6494
Fixes #7568 
Fixes #7385 
Fixes #7835 (mostly)
Fixes #7808 
Fixes #5865 

HMR is not working due to MV3 restrictions on CSP. Refreshing the page does update the extension though.

## ✔️ PR Todo

- [x] Added/updated unit tests for this change
- [x] Included links to related issues/PRs

I hope my issues are reproducible with the following descriptions. It might be possible that I somehow messed something up by building it myself and applying the patch via [patch-package](https://github.com/ds300/patch-package).

1. Specifying `web_accessible_resources` in a manifest v3 causes a build error.

```json
"web_accessible_resources": [{
    "resources": ["images/*"],
    "matches": ["<all_urls>"]
}],
```

The following error refers to [this line here](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/b71d9866bbf2e2434f665e2026669e31c2898950/packages/transformers/webextension/src/WebExtensionTransformer.js#L191).
```
@parcel/transformer-webextension: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received an instance of Array

  TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string. Received an instance of Array
  at new NodeError (node:internal/errors:372:5)
  at validateString (node:internal/validators:120:11)
  at Object.join (node:path:1172:7)
  at collectDependencies (@parcel/transformer-webextension/lib/WebExtensionTransformer.js:215:67)
  at Object.transform (@parcel/transformer-webextension/lib/WebExtensionTransformer.js:370:13)
```

2. ~~It seems like it's not possible to use `import` in the background service worker.~~ (whoops, my bad; see [response below](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/pull/7050#issuecomment-1071433977))

```json
"background": {
    "service_worker": "background.ts"
}
```

```
@parcel/transformer-js: Service workers cannot have imports or exports without the `type: "module"` option.

  background.ts:1:1
  > 1 | import browser from 'webextension-polyfill';
  >   | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
    2 | import optionsStorage from './options-storage.js';
    3 | 

  💡 Add {type: 'module'} as a second argument to the navigator.serviceWorker.register() call.
  📝 Learn more: https://parceljs.org/languages/javascript/#classic-scripts
```

> Specifying `web_accessible_resources` in a manifest v3 causes a build error.

This shouldn't happen, I'll fix that.

> It seems like it's not possible to use import in the background service worker.

It is but you need to specify that it's a module type service worker. This behavior is [consistent with browsers](https://stackoverflow.com/a/66408379/10930232).
```json
"background": {
    "service_worker": "background.ts",
    "type": "module"
}
```

@101arrowz I've encountered another issue while testing:

`content_scripts` are not resolved correctly. The paths should be relative to the manifest and not the CWD (current working directory).

Example:

`src/manifest.json`
```
"content_scripts": [
	{
		"matches": ["<all_urls>"],
		"js": ["inject.js"],
		"run_at": "document_start"
	}
],
```

`parcel watch src/manifest.json --dist-dir distribution --no-cache --no-hmr`

Error: `no such file or directory, open '/path/to/repo/inject.js'`

Expected: It should open `src/inject.js`
Actual: It opens `inject.js` and fails, because that's not the correct path.

From what I understand, node_module imports are only followed in JS whereas other types need to specifically use `"npm:package-name"`. So in this case `"file.js"` should still be supported and relative to the current file.

- https://parceljs.org/features/dependency-resolution/#url-schemes
- complete example in a CSS file: https://parceljs.org/languages/css/#%40import
- example without `./` in an HTML file: https://parceljs.org/languages/html/#scripts

> Doesn't that happen because it thinks inject.js is a module since there's no leading `./`?

Without the patch this works as expected (and this also worked the last time I tried this patch @ b71d986). The documentation also shows that it should work without leading `./`: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Add-ons/WebExtensions/manifest.json/content_scripts

After debugging a bit I found the issue. Apparently the function `asset.invalidateOnFileChange()` takes a path relative to the project root, while every other function takes a path relative to the asset's path. I wish this behavior were documented somewhere! Anyway it's fixed now.

issue_context.title: Support manifest v3 for web extensions
issue_context.body:
<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

# 🙋 feature request
Chrome (and Edge) support a newer version of the extension manifest, [v3](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/mv3-overview/) but the webextension config plugin only supports version 2. The two are very similar, but some of the fields that name resources are different.
<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue here -->

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

<!--- Tell us how the feature should work -->
The `@parcel/config-webextension` package should support extensions that are defined with v3 of the manifests (i.e. point `parcel` at the `manifest.json` and let it package things up).

## 😯 Current Behavior

<!--- Explain the difference from current behavior -->
Currently when following the [Web Extension recipe](https://v2.parceljs.org/recipes/web-extension/) and using a v3 manifest, `parcel build` throws an error:
```
@parcel/transformer-webextension: Invalid Web Extension manifest
/path/to/my/extension/manifest.json:5:23
  4 |   "version": "1.0",
> 5 |   "manifest_version": 3,
>   |                       ^ Possible values: "2"
  6 |   "action": {
  7 |     "default_popup": "popup.html"
  ```

## 💁 Possible Solution

<!--- Ideas how to implement this feature or a similar solution/workaround that already exists -->
From parcel's point of view, the manifests are fairly similar.
- The [schema check](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/a3aa86815e098c90fda72a08d29646ff059ab74d/packages/transformers/webextension/src/schema.js#L46) needs to allow version 3
- The new [`background.service_worker` property](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/getstarted/#background)
- The CSP setting has [changed from being a simple string](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/mv3-migration/#fcontent-security-policy) so the [HMR logic](https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/a3aa86815e098c90fda72a08d29646ff059ab74d/packages/transformers/webextension/src/WebExtensionTransformer.js#L241-L261) will need to be modified to rewrite multiple policies instead of just one.
- The actions, which can refer to resources, have [moved under a new toplevel key](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/mv3-migration/#action-api-unification)
- The schema for `web_accessible_resources` [changed slightly](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/mv3-migration/#web-accessible-resources)
- There are additional [restrictions on how code is executed](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/mv3-migration/#code-execution) and I do not know how this affects the bundles and HMR code for Parcel.

## 🔦 Context

<!--- How has this issue affected you? What are you trying to accomplish? -->

Chrome is pushing this as the new way to write extensions and has removed much of the v2 documentation in favor of [pushing v3 by default](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/). A big architecture change for extensions seems to be the move to [using service workers + message passing instead of a background page](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/migrating_to_service_workers/). I am starting to write a new extension (not having done so before), so I am trying to follow the documentation on the Chrome site and set this project up for having the right long-term architecture, so following the v3 manifest feels like the best course, rather than creating a v2 manifest.

<!--- Providing context helps us come up with a solution that is most useful in the real world -->

## 💻 Examples

<!-- Examples help us understand the requested feature better -->

There don't seem to be many official examples yet - even the official repo has a [limited selection](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/chrome-extensions-samples/blob/main/examples/hello-world/manifest.json).

<!-- Love parcel? Please consider supporting our collective:
👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->

I've run into a problem: the hack used to enable HMR in content scripts [is no longer possible](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/mv3/intro/mv3-migration/#content-security-policy).

> In addition, MV3 disallows certain CSP modifications for `extension_pages` that were permitted in MV2. The `script-src`, `object-src`, and `worker-src` directives may only have the following values:
> - `self`
> - `none`
> - Any localhost source, (`http://localhost`, `http://127.0.0.1`, or any port on those domains)

We need `unsafe-eval` so that `new Function(newCode)` can be used in the HMR code. This is a serious problem: one of the key benefits of the WebExtension transformer over not using a bundler at all is HMR. Is there any workaround?
I think I would like the support for v3 even without HMR. A workaround for HMR could be figured out after the fact if possible.

review_comments: Should there be some assertions about the content of the manifest? I.e. covering the stuff done by the packager/runtime, including injecting referenced bundle urls etc.
I wasn't sure how to deal with content hashing, is there a way to handle that?
Any kind of assertions are good. Like asserting the correct number of referenced files, some regex on the name, etc.
I added a few more tests that should hopefully cover most common use cases. Full testing of e.g. the HMR functionality would probably be a bit too cumbersome.
I guess this moved from the transformer into a runtime? I'm curious about why that was. Would you mind explaining a bit?

Sure. We needed to move to a runtime because there was no way to inject the autoreload into specifically the background pages or the service worker without adding another specialized transformer for those files, or hijacking the JS transformer. Of course, the original strategy of using the transformer for this worked fine for `background.scripts` users, but that is MV2.
I assume this empty script is needed for some reason?
Yes, we need it to inject the auto-reloader for content-script page refresh. That's `autoreload-bg.js` in the runtime.
